evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.25: virum bonum et nōn illitterātum (Lewis & Short)
Col. 1.8.4: of one who cannot read (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Seneca (Ben. 5.13.4, Lewis & Short) notes that it is used of one not wholly ignorant but not brought to higher letters; Columella uses it of one who cannot read (Lewis & Short).
From Greek analphabētos, not knowing the alphabet; not in Lewis & Short.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 30, checked against the searchable text of the book.: p. 331.
